items.title: (NeurIPS Dataset&Benchmark 2025) Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? [Paper
items.description: ] | Analyzes recurring failure modes in multi-agent systems and develops a taxonomy spanning agent design, coordination, and verification.

items.title: (ASE 2025 Distinguished Paper Award) Understanding Software Engineering Agents: A Study of Thought-Action-Result Trajectories [Paper
items.description: ] | Studies 120 trajectories and 2,822 LLM interactions, identifying recurring motifs, anti-patterns, token-use patterns, and feedback-integration agentic coding behavior.

items.title: (ASE-NIER 2025) Exploring autonomous agents: A closer look at why they fail when completing tasks [Paper
items.description: ] | Develops a three-tier taxonomy that characterizes autonomous-agent failures across task-planning, task-execution, and response-generation phases.

items.title: (arXiv 2026) Failure as a Process: An Anatomy of CLI Coding Agent Trajectories [Paper
items.description: ] | Studies failure as a developing process across CLI-agent trajectories.

items.title: Empirical Study/Characterization
(ICML 2025 Spotlight) Which Agent Causes Task Failures and When? On Automated Failure Attribution of LLM Multi-Agent Systems [Paper
items.description: ] | Formalizes automated failure attribution at both the agent and step levels and introduces the Who&When benchmark.

items.title: (arXiv 2026) AgentRx: Diagnosing AI Agent Failures from Execution Trajectories [Paper
items.description: ] | Synthesizes and checks step-wise constraints to diagnose root causes and pinpoint the earliest unrecoverable point in failed executions.

items.title: (ICLR 2026) AgenTracer: Who Is Inducing Failure in the LLM Agentic Systems? [Paper
items.description: ] | Trains an AgenTracer-8B via counterfactual replay and programmed fault injection to attribute failures to responsible agents or trajectory segments.

items.title: (ACL 2026) Seeing the Whole Elephant: A Benchmark for Failure Attribution in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems [Paper
items.description: ] | Introduces TraceElephant, a benchmark and evaluation framework that captures complete multi-agent execution traces for assessing failure attribution across agents, interactions, and time steps.

items.title: (arXiv 2025) Abduct, Act, Predict: Scaffolding Causal Inference for Automated Failure Attribution in Multi-Agent Systems [Paper
items.description: ] | Uses abductive reasoning, interventions, and predictions to causally attribute multi-agent failures.

items.title: (arXiv 2026) TrajAudit: Automated Failure Diagnosis for Agentic Coding Systems [Paper
items.description: ] | Uses an investigator agent with context-reduction mechanisms to localize the earliest decisive error step in repository-level coding-agent trajectories and generate diagnostic justifications.

items.title: (arXiv 2026) StepFinder: A Temporal Semantic Framework for Failure Attribution in Multi-Agent Systems [Paper
items.description: ] | Encodes execution logs into temporal semantic sequences with an LLM, then uses lightweight temporal modeling and attention over the sequence to score and localize the root-cause step, cutting inference time by 79% versus the fastest LLM-based baseline.

items.title: Failure Localization, Attribution, and Diagnosis
(ACL 2026) ReCreate: Reasoning and Creating Domain Agents Driven by Experience [Paper
items.description: ] | Uses accumulated execution experience to construct and refine domain-specific agents.

items.title: (arXiv 2025) SCOPE: Prompt Evolution for Enhancing Agent Effectiveness [Paper
items.description: ] | Uses trajectory feedback to evolve prompts and improve future agent performance.

items.title: (arXiv 2026) Trace2Skill: Distill Trajectory-Local Lessons into Transferable Agent Skills [Paper
items.description: ] | Extracts local lessons from execution traces and converts them into reusable skills.

items.title: Learning and Optimization from Trajectories
(arXiv 2026) AdaRubric: Task-Adaptive Rubrics for Reliable LLM Agent Evaluation and Reward Learning [Paper
items.description: ] | Dynamically generates task-specific rubrics to evaluate agent trajectories step by step and produce confidence-weighted preference data for reward learning.

items.title: (arXiv 2026) AgentProcessBench: Diagnosing Step-Level Process Quality in Tool-Using Agents [Paper
items.description: ] | Introduces human-annotated trajectories and methods for evaluating the quality of individual reasoning and tool-use steps.

items.title: (arXiv 2026) MAESTRO: Multi-Agent Evaluation Suite for Testing, Reliability, and Observability [Paper
items.description: ] | Provides evaluation dimensions and testing infrastructure for multi-agent reliability and observability.

items.title: (arXiv 2026) ARCO: Adaptive Rubric with Co-Evolution for Multi-Step LLM-Based Agents [Paper
items.description: ] | Introduces a co-evolution framework that jointly improves an agent and a hierarchical rubric model to provide interpretable step-level process rewards for multi-step trajectories.

items.title: (ACL-Findings 2026) ToolPRMBench: Evaluating and Advancing Process Reward Models for Tool-using Agents [Paper
items.description: ] | Introduces a large-scale benchmark of structured, step-level test cases for evaluating and advancing process reward models in tool-using agent scenarios.

items.title: (arXiv 2026) Agent Step Value: State-Transition Measurement with State-Grounded LLM Evaluators [Paper
items.description: ] | Measures the value of each agent action by evaluating the change it induces between consecutive environment states with state-grounded LLM evaluators.

items.title: Trajectory Quality Assessment
(PACMI 2025) AgentSight: System-Level Observability for AI Agents Using eBPF [Paper
items.description: ] | Applies system-level telemetry to observe agent interactions with tools, processes, and runtime environments.

items.title: (arXiv 2026) CodeTracer: Towards Traceable Agent States [Paper
items.description: ] | Introduces explicit representations of coding-agent states to support stage- and step-level failure tracing.

items.title: (arXiv 2026) GRADE: Graph Representation of LLM Agent Dependency and Execution [Paper
items.description: ] | Models an agent run as a two-layer graph with execution edges and dependency edges graded, to predict failure likelihood and localize the faulting step.

items.title: Trajectory Representation
Trajectory Benchmarks and Datasets
ClawBench [Paper
items.description: ] [Code] [Data] | Real-world browser-agent benchmark releasing five-layer run artifacts: MP4 replay, screenshots, HTTP requests, browser actions, and agent messages.

items.title: Who&When [Paper
items.description: ] | 127 multi-agent trajectories annotated with the responsible agent and the time at which the failure was introduced.

items.title: AgentErrorBench [Paper
items.description: ] | 200 multi-agent/embodied executions (ALFWorld, GAIA, WebShop) annotated under the AgentErrorTaxonomy for failure analysis and attribution.

items.title: Aegis [Paper
items.description: ] | 9,533 trajectories across diverse MAS architectures and task domains, automatically labeled with faulty agents and error modes via an LLM-based error injector, supporting SFT, RL, and contrastive-learning training paradigms.

items.title: MP-Bench [Paper
items.description: ] | Multi-perspective attribution data (289 instances) containing per-annotator failure-reason and ideal-action annotations.
